prompt:
Scene:
A top-down square photograph of the same open cream-paper journal from the reference, now very late at night under a warm yellow desk lamp. The surrounding desk fades into soft shadow, and the right page is brighter than the left because the lamp sits off to the right. A half-empty mug sits just outside the frame casting a small warm reflection on the page corner.

Subject:
The same journal keeper's closing page of the week. The left page has a dreamy charcoal smudge of a night sky, a ticket stub from a late-night cinema taped down, and a few stars drawn in small off-center marks. The right page is a long, tired block of slanted ballpoint writing that drifts more than earlier pages, a bleeding fountain-pen underline, and a single long strip of terracotta washi tape running diagonally across one corner with a visible fingerprint smudge from pressing it down.

Important details:
Preserve exact identity of the journal from the reference: same cream paper tone, same A5 proportions, same binding curve, same handwriting cadence (even more uneven now due to tiredness — one letter genuinely wobbles mid-line), same terracotta washi tape, same navy ballpoint, plus a new fountain-pen ink bleed that hints the writer switched pens late in the night. Only the mood, light, and pasted ephemera change. The lamp glow falls off realistically, not as a vignette filter.

Use case:
Series image 4 of 4 · the final page of the week, closing the emotional arc of the same physical notebook.

Constraints:
No readable text, no watermark, no logos, no brand names, no vignette filter, no clean symmetry, no glossy surface, no sharp digital glow, preserve exact 1:1 aspect ratio.
